newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firms as Buba drains 2.0 bln dmk.
newsitem.headline: German call money firms as Buba drains 2.0 bln dmk.

text.p: German call money rates ticked higher on Wednesday, tightening to between 3.10 and 3.15 percent after the Bundesbank drained 2.0 billion marks in its weekly repo operation.
Traders said that before the bank operated, call money was centred around the 3.07 level, but a larger than forecast drainage had pushed the rate up slightly.
"After the Bundesbank gave us less money than we expected, the rates moved slightly higher," said a trader in Frankfurt.

The Bundesbank earlier said it had allocated 82 billion marks in 14-day securities repurchase funds at a fixed rate of three percent. At the same time, a repo pact for 84.0 billion marks also expired at the same rate.
Analysts had been expecting a one billion mark drain on the market.

"I think that the Bundesbank thinks something will come through in terms of cash flow after the Easter holidays, but we still haven't seen that," said another dealer. "So as a result rates are a little higher and the market is looking for funds."

On Tuesday, banks held 40.8 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank, down from 42.2 billion held on Monday. Holdings for the month also slipped to 41.8 billion marks from from 42.0 billion on Monday.
No appreciable amount was borrowed on the 4.50 percent Lombard financing window. The Frankfurt interbank overnight rate stood at 3.15000 percent versus 3.12567 on Tuesday.
